A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VidMuse and V2M. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support comparison across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, a 40-participant user study, and architectural and training ablations in the main text and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, retained user-study outcomes, and revised ablation results, including newly reported encoder computational costs.

M1.justification: Both retain visual encoding, long/short-term modeling with cross-attention fusion, autoregressive music-token prediction, codec decoding, cross-entropy training, and sliding-window inference. v2 provides additional architectural detail without establishing a new component or algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 Section 3.1 incorporates HIMV-200K and Music/Trailer-tagged YouTube-8M videos into the training collection, broadening v1's query-collected pool. The video-to-music task and 300-pair V2M-bench evaluation remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v1 Table 1 and v2 Table 2 evaluate the same Caption2Music, Video2Music, CMT, M2UGen, and VM-NET comparators. User-study participants' comparison methods and architectural-ablation variants also match.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes pretraining from 190K to 360K samples, training from 22,000 to 56,000 steps, and the 30-second inference window's overlap from 5 to 0.5 seconds. v2 also introduces GFLOPs in the encoder comparison. These constitute substantial reported setting changes.

E4.justification: The encoder ablation adds computational-cost analysis, and the finetuning-size analysis receives revised evidence. v1's training and benchmark duration-distribution analyses disappear. Design-choice, model-size, FPS/duration, and codebook studies remain, with several relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for generation results. The user study retains 40 participants, 60 comparisons per method pair, and preference-percentage reporting.

E6.justification: v2 Table 2 replaces VidMuse's scores, including FD 36.171 to 29.946, FAD 2.369 to 2.459, and ImageBind 0.207 to 0.202. Every finetuning row changes; CLIP scores change and encoder GFLOPs appear. Several encoder/model-size metric entries disappear. Changed training settings prevent interpreting these as controlled performance improvements; baseline and user-study scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The refined-feature definitions change from dimensions involving the attention-head count N_H in v1 Section 4.3 to explicit frame, patch, and feature axes in v2 Section 4.1. Training also distinguishes vocabulary logits and one-hot targets. These are limited revisions to the formal specification; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list enlarge the claimed dataset from 190K to 360K pairs. The central video-only generation contribution, local/global modeling claim, and claimed superiority in quality, diversity, and alignment remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 attributes CMT's silence to slowly changing or static frames instead of v1's darker segments, and removes discussion of M2UGen's stitching discontinuities. It elaborates why identical clips may require different music in different global contexts. The codec, computational-resource, and ImageBind limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds block-level architecture details in Figure 4, decoder-conditioning and target descriptions, and a user-study interface in Figure A1. It omits v1's 48-GPU count and explicit 'official trailer' query suffix. Code and dataset access remains a promised release at the same address.

R1.justification: v2 adds MeLFusion and Diff-BGM while removing several background references, including Jukebox and the RVQGAN codec work. The four-part related-work organization and positioning around video-only generation with local/global context largely remain.

P1.justification: The method section is substantially rewritten and consolidated into architecture, training, and discussion. Dataset-filtering details, metric explanations, and inference move into expanded appendices; encoder and input ablations exchange main-text/appendix placement. Extensive wording, heading, citation-style, and author-list edits accompany this reorganization.

P2.justification: v2 adds the detailed LSTV diagram, user-study interface, and dataset-statistics table. It redraws dataset plots, removes duration histograms, rearranges four user-study heatmaps into one row, compresses model/encoder tables, and relocates the input-ablation table and spectrogram comparison.

improvement.justification: v2 improves architectural clarity and supplies encoder computational costs, but removes useful ablation metrics and introduces unresolved dataset reporting problems. Its 20,000 finetuning videos total 6,000 hours in Table 1, implying 1,080 seconds per video despite Appendix A.2's 480-second maximum; v1 reported 597 hours. These documentation gains and reporting losses leave the net quality change uncertain.
